title: Museums for peace: Decolonial museology of painful heritage in Colombia
abstract: Colonial structures in knowledge production have hindered recognition of decolonial practices in memory work and museums as agents of social transformation. “Museums for Peace” is a research initiative focused on community-based memory museums in Colombia. Its framework draws on critical, social, and community-based museologies, alongside decolonial and feminist perspectives on knowledge production and emotions. The initiative explored museological contributions to peacebuilding through a two-stage methodology addressing memory work around violent pasts linked to colonization and armed conflict. Engaged research with three civil society organizations identified four emergent factors: focus on socio-economic causes of violence; integration of traditional and performative museographic practices; debate over communities as sources versus experts as knowledge producers; and critical engagement with memory’s normative framework. We define decolonial museums as spaces that challenge colonial tendencies to relegate painful memories, engaging instead with the multiplicity of heritage as a tool for reflection and peacebuilding.
